_doc: The kitchen gardens this scene draws (T-3407): each garden's beds and walks, in its own plan frame (u east from the west paling, v north from the south, metres; frame.origin is plan (0, 0) in local ENU metres of data/datum.json), and what grows in them. GENERATED by tools/plant_gardens.py from the garden's structure record and Whistler's 1808 draught -- do not hand-edit; re-run the tool. plants: {kind: [[e, n, yaw_deg, scale, variant], ...]} in local ENU. Drawn by renderers/web/js/gardens.js.
layout_note: The beds and walks are Whistler's 1808 draught's, measured off the pinned sheet and carried into the garden's box at its lettered scale: inferred, since that scale is read and the box itself is placed by rule. The scene's other gardens (T-3477) are laid out for their households by tools/plant_gardens_1812.py: reconstructed, each garden's own grade saying whether the garden itself is attested.

muskmelon.name: musk-melons
muskmelon.note: Quaife: in the commanding officer's gardens 'melons and other small fruit and vegetables were raised'. Hills six feet every way (M'Mahon), the fruit ripening on the vine in mid-August.

watermelon.name: water-melons
watermelon.note: Melons are Quaife's. Water-melons in hills nine or ten feet apart (M'Mahon).

currant.name: red currant bushes
currant.note: Small fruit is Quaife's; which small fruit is ours. Currants were picked in July, so a few strings are left.

gooseberry.name: gooseberry bushes
gooseberry.note: Small fruit is Quaife's; which small fruit is ours.

raspberry.name: raspberry canes
raspberry.note: Small fruit is Quaife's; which small fruit is ours. Last year's canes stand spent among this year's.

strawberry.name: strawberries
strawberry.note: Small fruit is Quaife's; which small fruit is ours. In August only leaves and runners.

cabbage.name: cabbages and savoys
cabbage.note: M'Mahon's August work: plant the last savoys two feet every way; earth up the cabbages.

corn.name: Indian corn
corn.note: Garden Indian corn in drills six feet apart, two stalks to a hill every two and a half feet (M'Mahon), tasselled and silking in August.

pole_bean.name: running beans on poles
pole_bean.note: Running kidney-beans in drills four or five feet asunder, on poles (M'Mahon), in leaf and pod.

potato.name: potatoes
potato.note: Earthed up in hills, the tops beginning to yellow.

squash.name: squashes and pumpkins
squash.note: Hills ten feet apart (M'Mahon), the fruit turning.

cucumber.name: cucumbers
cucumber.note: M'Mahon's August: melons and cucumbers 'in an advancing or fruiting state'.

onion.name: onions
onion.note: In drills; in August half their tops have fallen over, the sign they are ripe.

lettuce.name: lettuce and endive
lettuce.note: M'Mahon's August: transplant the advancing lettuces; tie up the full-grown endive.

asparagus.name: asparagus
asparagus.note: In its summer fern, the cutting long over.

herb.name: sage and thyme
herb.note: M'Mahon's August: cut the herbs in flower to dry for winter.

turnip.name: turnips, just sown
turnip.note: M'Mahon's August: 'The first week in this month, is a very principal time for sowing your general crops of turnep'; by the middle of the month the drills show their seed leaves.

weed.name: weeds: ragweed, lamb's-quarters, smartweed
weed.note: An annual weed stand on ground tilled last year and not this: waist to head high by August.

gardens.name: Kinzie's kitchen garden
gardens.where: North of the Kinzie house, inside its paling, the gate on the south toward the yard
gardens.household: John and Eleanor Kinzie, their four children and the household's servants and engagés
gardens.why: The largest and best-kept garden on the bank: a full kitchen range in two rows of beds either side of a walk from the gate, and the 'shrubbery' J. H. Kinzie remembered as a border of currants and gooseberries under the north paling.

gardens.name: Ouilmette's garden
gardens.where: Behind Antoine Ouilmette's house, west of Kinzie's horse mill
gardens.household: Antoine Ouilmette, his Potawatomi wife Archange, their children and Mrs. Bisson
gardens.why: Smaller and plainer than Kinzie's, and currant-heavy: the bushes the sergeant hid behind on 17 August, two rows of them already standing (data/flora/plantings/ouilmette_garden_1812.json) and more planted round them, then hill corn with beans and squash among it, potatoes and onions.

gardens.name: La Lime's dooryard patch
gardens.where: Behind the interpreter Jean La Lime's house
gardens.household: Jean La Lime's household; La Lime himself killed by Kinzie in June 1812
gardens.why: Planted in May and neglected since June, when its head was killed: corn hills going to weeds, the squash vines sprawling, lamb's-quarters and purslane between the hills. Who lived in the house after him is not known.

gardens.name: The Burns family's garden
gardens.where: A clearing behind the Burns cabin on the north bank, above the bank path
gardens.household: Burns, a discharged soldier, his wife and their children, the youngest born in April
gardens.why: A soldier-settler's subsistence patch cut out of the woods, rougher than any garden on the bank: potatoes, corn in hills, pumpkins, cabbages and beans, in uneven beds.

gardens.why: The draught draws a yard lettered 'Paling' east of the factory and says nothing of its use. A government official's household garden, kept neat: cabbages, onions, beans, salad, herbs and a melon bed.

gardens.name: The sutler's garden
gardens.where: Between the fort and the river mouth, inside its paling
gardens.household: The post's sutler, who sold to the soldiers
gardens.why: Lettered 'a Sutlers Garden' on the draught. A market garden for the garrison: a walk down the middle and four blocks of beds a side, plainer and more of a production garden than the officers', with no small fruit. Its north end is left to the way worn in from the fort road to the house the draught draws inside it.

gardens.name: Coursoll's field
gardens.where: North of the river, inside its worm fence, by Le Mai's house
gardens.household: Le Mai's household; the field is 'Coursoll's' on the draught
gardens.why: Quaife's 'house and inclosed field north of the river, belonging to Mr. Coursoll'. No crop is named: Indian corn in hills three and a half feet apart, a pumpkin in every third hill, the creole field's 'Corn, pumpkins, and spring wheat' (Brackenridge) less the wheat.

gardens.name: The little enclosure at Lee's Place
gardens.where: On the river side of the cabin at Lee's Place, on the South Branch
gardens.household: Nobody since April: White and Cardin killed there, the soldier and the boy fled
gardens.why: The 'small enclosure' the corporal jumped over in April (Wau-Bun ch. XVIII). The owner's ruling (2026-11-07): the place is left unplanted in 1812. Four months untended, it is a stand of weeds over the last pot-herbs, with a volunteer pumpkin.
